title: [VSC-11] VS Code: Release Agent action in task detail, matching JetBrains
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). Depends on VSC-6 (task-9f6a725ff14c4c08b4acb203884e7ae5), which adds MoeDaemonClient.releaseTask(taskId, reason?) for RELEASE_TASK.

Objective: JetBrains lets the human free a seat from the task detail dialog (TaskDetailDialog.kt) and the board card (MoeToolWindowPanel.handleReleaseAgent). The action shows only when task.assignedWorkerId is non-blank; it asks a Yes/No question titled "Release Agent" (moe.message.releaseAgentTitle) with the moe.message.releaseAgent text (MoeBundle.properties: `Release agent "{0}" from "{1}"? ...`, worker id then task title); on Yes it sends releaseTask(task.id, "Released from board") (moe.message.releasedInUI). VS Code has no equivalent.

Deliverable: in moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts, a "Release Agent" button rendered only when assignedWorkerId is non-blank, and a 'releaseAgent' message handler that shows a modal warning with JetBrains' text and calls client.releaseTask(taskId, 'Released from board') only on confirmation, showing a not-connected warning when it returns false (as the reopen handler already does); in moe-vscode/media/taskDetail.js, the button posting {type:'releaseAgent'}; new moe-vscode/tests/task-release.test.cjs.

Harness trap: three peer test files load TaskDetailPanel.ts with strict client stubs and require maps (mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness). Touch the new client member only inside the message handler, and add no value import.

TaskDetailPanel.ts is shared with VSC-8 and VSC-9: in shared-checkout mode do not run concurrently with them; after the worktree switch they merge independently.

Not in scope: a board-card release action (a follow-up if wanted), MoeDaemonClient.ts (VSC-6 owns it), any moe-jetbrains file.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh directory outside the checkout, overlay this task's files, then in <snapshot>/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).
definitionOfDone: moe-vscode/tests/task-release.test.cjs renders the real TaskDetailPanel HTML and asserts the Release Agent button is present for assignedWorkerId 'w1' and absent for null, empty and whitespace-only ids.

Driving the panel's message handler with {type:'releaseAgent'}: confirming calls client.releaseTask exactly once with (taskId, 'Released from board'); dismissing calls it zero times; a false return shows the not-connected warning.

The confirmation text equals moe.message.releaseAgent from moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties with the worker id and task title substituted, read from that file in the test.
task-blocker-visibility, task-time-budget and approval-paths pass unchanged.
In a git-archive snapshot of HEAD plus this diff, `cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 with 0 failures.

implementationPlan.description:
Write moe-vscode/tests/task-release.test.cjs FIRST, with the Write tool; it is red until steps 2-3 land. Copy the harness shapes into this file, never requiring a peer test:
- transpile, strict, loadModule and panelDependencies with `vscode` and `./PlanReviewPanel` from tests/task-blocker-visibility.test.cjs;
- loadDetailPage, makeNode and initialDataset from tests/approval-paths.test.cjs.
mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness and mem:convention-vscode-renderer-tests cover the realm traps: compare vm-realm objects field by field or through JSON, never with deepStrictEqual.
- Fake vscode: window.createWebviewPanel returns a fake panel whose webview captures the onDidReceiveMessage listener. window.showWarningMessage, showInformationMessage and showErrorMessage are recorders; showWarningMessage returns a per-test answer.
- Fake client: a strict proxy with currentState, onStateChanged, onError, onConnectionChanged and a releaseTask recorder that returns a per-test boolean.
- Fixture: a makeTask with id 'task-release' and title `Ship "release" <fast> & safe`, so the test proves the modal text is NOT HTML-escaped.
- Read MoeBundle.properties as UTF-8 from `path.join(__dirname, '../../moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties')` with `/^moe\.(button\.releaseAgent|message\.releaseAgent|message\.releasedInUI)=(.*?)\r?$/gm`. Assert moe.message.releaseAgent holds no single quote, so a plain {0}/{1} substitution equals Java MessageFormat.
Its error handling: a missing bundle line fails with a message naming the key.
Tests:
1. Button: the real panel HTML (createOrShow) holds `<button class="btn btn-secondary" id="releaseAgentBtn">` + the bundle's moe.button.releaseAgent + `</button>` for assignedWorkerId 'w1'. It holds no `id="releaseAgentBtn"` for null, '' or '   '.
2. Confirm: invoke the captured listener with {type:'releaseAgent'} and await it, with the warning recorder answering the bundle's moe.button.releaseAgent.
   - showWarningMessage got exactly (text, an options object whose modal === true, 'Release Agent'), where text = the bundle's moe.message.releaseAgent with {0} replaced by 'w1' and {1} by the raw title;
   - releaseTask was called exactly once with ('task-release', the bundle's moe.message.releasedInUI = 'Released from board');
   - no error message was shown.
3. Dismiss: the recorder answers undefined. releaseTask is called zero times and nothing else is shown.
4. Not connected: confirm, with releaseTask returning false. The second showWarningMessage call is exactly 'Not connected to Moe daemon — agent was not released.'
5. Stale button: after rendering with 'w1', set currentState's task assignedWorkerId to null and invoke the listener. There is no modal and no releaseTask call, and showInformationMessage gets exactly 'No agent is assigned to this task.'
6. Page wiring: loadDetailPage(rendered HTML) with a getElementById that returns null for an id absent from the HTML (as a real DOM does). For 'w1', click('releaseAgentBtn') posts exactly [{type:'releaseAgent'}]. For an unassigned task the page loads without throwing and posts nothing.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The handler reads the task fresh at click time, because the VS Code actions bar is static: approve, reject and reopen share that staleness, and the daemon is the final arbiter. Rejected: a live show/hide of the button through taskDetail.js. It would need an always-rendered hidden button, which conflicts with DoD 1's 'absent', and the other buttons are static anyway. Rejected: a VS Code-specific title in the modal. VS Code's modal has no title line, so the JetBrains text is the message and 'Release Agent' is the confirm item. No success toast, matching JetBrains.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: TaskDetailPanel value-imports only vscode and ./PlanReviewPanel. Its message listener returns the handler's Promise, so a test can await it. nonBlankString already exists in the module. task-time-budget's fixture is assigned to worker-1, so its HTML gains the button; its assertions only target regions, so it should stay green. approval-paths' getElementById creates nodes on demand, so the new test needs a null-for-absent variant to prove the guard.
planningNotes.risks: The bundle text contains an em dash: read the properties file as UTF-8 and keep the dash in the TS constant. The vm-realm options object ({modal:true}) needs a field comparison. VSC-6 must be DONE before a worker can claim this row (dependsOn). TaskDetailPanel.ts is shared with VSC-9. HEAD can carry a peer's red wip checkpoint (mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint).

completionSummary:

Only on confirm does it call client.releaseTask(taskId, 'Released from board'); a false return shows 'Not connected to Moe daemon — agent was not released.'. No success toast, as in JetBrains.
